title: The Constricted Field: Clinical Mastery
summary: A comprehensive guide to 'tunnel vision' and peripheral field loss, ranging from end-stage glaucoma and tapetoretinal degenerations to neurological and functional etiologies. Essential for board-prep and advanced ophthalmic practice.

sections.title: Definition & Clinical Overview
sections.content: Constricted visual fields, colloquially termed 'tunnel vision', involve the loss of peripheral vision while retaining a small central island (typically <10–20°). This can result from end-stage optic neuropathies, retinal dystrophies, or cortical insults. Clinically, it significantly impacts mobility and orientation, while central visual acuity often remains remarkably preserved (20/20) until the terminal stages.

sections.title: Pathophysiology Mechanisms
content: Step 1: Peripheral Photoreceptor or Ganglion Cell death (Retrograde/Anterograde degeneration).
Step 2: Microvascular compromise in the watershed zones of the peripheral retina.
Step 3: Glial proliferation (gliosis) and RPE migration (Bone Spicules).
Step 4: Optic nerve remodeling and axonal loss at the Lamina Cribrosa.

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Optic Disc: Cupping (Glaucoma), Waxy Pallor (RP), or Chronic Swelling/Atrophy (Papilledema).
Vessels: Arteriolar attenuation (characteristic of RP and long-standing atrophy).
Retina: Bone-spicule pigmentation in the mid-periphery (RP), or sector-based atrophy.
Macula: Often spared until late stages; check for Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) in RP.
Gonioscopy: Assess for Angle-Closure (synechiae) as a cause of rapid field loss.

sections.title: CRITICAL EMERGENCY SIGNS
content: Sudden onset peripheral loss (Vascular Occlusion/Retinal Detachment)
New onset headache and disc edema (Intracranial Hypertension)
Temporal artery tenderness (GCA - can cause ischemic optic neuropathy)
Rapidly progressive field loss in an only eye
Presence of neurological deficits (Hemiparesis/Ataxia)

sections.title: Investigations & Workup
content: 1. Static Perimetry (HVF 24-2/30-2): Initial assessment of depth and pattern.
2. Kinetic Perimetry (Goldmann): Gold standard for peripheral constriction and 'tubular' testing.
3. 10-2 Perimetry: Crucial for monitoring the remaining central island.
4. OCT (RNFL and GCL): Quantify structural loss; follow-up for progression.
5. Electroretinogram (fERG/mfERG): Differentiate retinal (RP) from neural (Optic Nerve) causes.
6. Neuro-imaging (MRI Brain/Orbits): Mandatory if field loss does not match clinical exam or is neurological.

content.explanation: P: Papilledema (Chronic Stage); U: Uveitis (Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada late); R: Retinitis Pigmentosa; G: Glaucoma (End-stage); E: Embolus (CRAO with cilioretinal sparing).

sections.title: Surgical & Medical Management
content: Medical (Glaucoma): PG Analogs (Latanoprost 0.005% QHS), Beta-blockers (Timolol 0.5% BID).
Surgical (Glaucoma): Trabeculectomy with Mitomycin-C or GDD (Ahmed/Baerveldt) to stabilize field.
Gene Therapy: Voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) for RPE65-mediated RP.
Systemic: Acetazolamide for chronic papilledema; weight loss (IIH).
Vitamins: Vitamin A Palmitate (15,000 IU/day) for RP (consult specialist first).

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Trabeculectomy
content: 1. Conjunctival peritomy (limbal or fornix based).
2. Partial thickness scleral flap creation.
3. Application of Mitomycin-C (0.2-0.4 mg/ml) for 2-3 minutes.
4. Sclerostomy and peripheral iridectomy.
5. Flap closure with 10-0 Nylon (releasable or fixed).

content.explanation: Sudden loss of the remaining central island after glaucoma surgery. Occurs in end-stage patients with <10 degrees of field.

rows: Tubes vs. Trab for previous failure.

sections.title: Toxic & Nutritional Causes
content: Quinine Toxicity: Can lead to profound peripheral constriction.
Vigabatrin: Anti-epileptic causing irreversible peripheral VF loss (requires baseline perimetry).
Ethambutol: Usually central/cecocentral but can cause generalized depression.
Methanol: Severe optic atrophy and field constriction.

sections.title: Pediatric & Special Populations
sections.content: In children, constricted fields often point towards Leber Congenital Amaurosis (LCA) or syndromes like Usher's (sensorineural hearing loss + RP). Testing is difficult; utilize FPL (Formatted Preferential Looking) and objective electrophysiology (ERG) early to assess potential for low vision rehabilitation.
